# One template file, two deployment modes, no edits

The same template file runs against an all-in-one deployment and against a
split, multi-container deployment. There is no dev-versus-prod template dialect.

## The template

Nothing about the file refers to a deployment shape.

```yaml
name: portable-across-modes
version: "1"
description: |
  One template file, run unedited against an all-in-one deployment and
  against a multi-container deployment.
nodes:
  - type: verifier
    executor: verifier-shape-checks
    attributes:
      schema:
        type: object
        properties:
          checks:
            type: array
            default:
              - kind: no_nulls
                config:
                  field: id
              - kind: pk_unique
                config:
                  field: id
          rows:
            type: array
            default:
              - id: alpha
                value: 1
              - id: beta
                value: 2
        required: [checks, rows]
```

## Mode one: the all-in-one deployment

```bash
docker run -d -p 8080:8080 rimsky-all-in-one:<tag>

rimsky run --endpoint http://127.0.0.1:8080 template.yml
rimsky watch --endpoint http://127.0.0.1:8080 "$INSTANCE_ID"
```

Its baked zero-config SQLite defaults are enough.

## Mode two: the split deployment

A database container, a bundled-executor container, and three role containers
sharing one configuration:

```bash
docker run -d --network rimsky-net --network-alias db postgres:...
docker run -d --network rimsky-net --network-alias shapes \
  rimsky-executor-verifier-shape-checks:<tag>

docker run -d --network rimsky-net -p 8081:8080 \
  -v "$PWD/rimsky.yml:/etc/rimsky/rimsky.yml:ro" \
  rimsky:<tag> rimsky-control-api
docker run -d --network rimsky-net \
  -v "$PWD/rimsky.yml:/etc/rimsky/rimsky.yml:ro" \
  rimsky:<tag> rimsky-scheduler
docker run -d --network rimsky-net \
  -v "$PWD/rimsky.yml:/etc/rimsky/rimsky.yml:ro" \
  rimsky:<tag> rimsky-supervisor
```

Run the same file:

```bash
rimsky run --endpoint http://127.0.0.1:8081 template.yml
rimsky watch --endpoint http://127.0.0.1:8081 "$INSTANCE_ID"
```

## What the product does

On each deployment the file registers, deploys, instantiates, reaches a terminal
state, and leaves every node with one fresh run. `rimsky watch` returns 0 in
each.

Two things rule out a false pass. The file's own hash is unchanged after both
runs, so nothing rewrote it for the second mode. And both deployments
content-address it to the same template hash, so each accepted the identical
bytes rather than a normalization of its own.
